websocket.serverOpen.description: Runs when another program connects to one of your own WebSocket servers. A WebSocket is an open line two programs use to chat quickly.

fields.server: Only run for the WebSocket server with this name (a server you made in Cuebot that other programs can connect to). Leave empty for any server.

websocket.serverMessage.description: Runs when a program connected to your own WebSocket server sends Cuebot a message.

fields.server: Only run for the WebSocket server with this name (a server you made in Cuebot that other programs can connect to). Leave empty for any server.

websocket.serverClose.description: Runs when a program disconnects from one of your own WebSocket servers.

fields.server: Only run for the WebSocket server with this name (a server you made in Cuebot that other programs can connect to). Leave empty for any server.

websocket.clientOpen.description: Runs when Cuebot connects to another program over a WebSocket (an open line two programs use to chat quickly).

fields.client: Only run for the WebSocket client with this name (a connection Cuebot makes to another program). Leave empty for any client.

websocket.clientMessage.description: Runs when the other program, which Cuebot is connected to over a WebSocket, sends Cuebot a message.

fields.client: Only run for the WebSocket client with this name (a connection Cuebot makes to another program). Leave empty for any client.

websocket.clientClose.description: Runs when Cuebot's WebSocket connection to another program ends.

fields.client: Only run for the WebSocket client with this name (a connection Cuebot makes to another program). Leave empty for any client.

variables.reason: Why it ended: disconnected (on purpose) or closed (by the other side)

webhook.custom.description: Runs when another app or website visits a web link you made in Cuebot (a custom hook). Use it to start actions from your own tools.

fields.hookName: Only run for the hook with this name. Leave empty to run for every hook you made.
fields.includeTests: Tick to also run for test events (made with a "send test" button). Untick to run only for real ones.

variables.method: How it was called, like GET or POST
variables.query: The extra bits added after the ? in the link
variables.body: The text that was sent along
variables.contentType: What kind of data was sent
variables.isTest: True when this is a test event, not a real one
variables.query.NAME: Each item in the link's ? part, by its name

custom.codeEvent.description: Runs when a script, another action or a connected program fires a custom event with a name you choose. A way to chain your own actions.

fields.eventName: Only run for the event with this name, like "BossFight". Leave empty to run for every custom event.

variables.eventName: The name of the event that was fired

ifttt.notificationBasic.description: Tells IFTTT that something happened, with one line of text. IFTTT can then do anything you set up, like flash a smart light.

fields.eventName: The event name you chose in your IFTTT applet, like "stream_alert".
fields.text: The text to send. Your IFTTT applet receives it as Value1.
fields.key: Your IFTTT Webhooks key. Leave empty to use the key already saved in Cuebot. Find it on ifttt.com/maker_webhooks.

ifttt.notificationAdvanced.description: Tells IFTTT that something happened, with several named pieces of information. IFTTT can then act on them.

fields.eventName: The event name you chose in your IFTTT applet, like "stream_alert".
fields.arguments: One per line, written as name=value, like score=10. IFTTT gets the first five as Argument1Name, Argument1Value and so on, and all of them together as ArgumentsJson.
fields.key: Your IFTTT Webhooks key. Leave empty to use the key already saved in Cuebot. Find it on ifttt.com/maker_webhooks.

websocket.serverSend.description: Sends a message to programs connected to one of your own WebSocket servers (an open line to another app). Use it to talk to your own tools.

fields.server: Which server: its name, or its number in your list (0 is the first).
fields.sessionId: Send to just one connected program: type its session id. Leave empty to send to all. In a message trigger, %sessionId% answers whoever wrote.

variables.sentCount: How many programs got the message

websocket.serverState.description: Starts or stops one of your own WebSocket servers (the open line other programs connect to).

fields.server: Which server: its name, or its number in your list (0 is the first).
fields.state: Start opens the server, Stop closes it.

websocket.clientSend.description: Sends a message to another program over a WebSocket connection Cuebot has made. Fails if the connection is not open.

fields.client: Which client: its name, or its number in your list (0 is the first).

websocket.clientState.description: Connects Cuebot to another program over a WebSocket, or ends that connection.

fields.client: Which client: its name, or its number in your list (0 is the first).
fields.state: Connect opens the connection, Disconnect closes it.

websocket.broadcast.description: Sends a message to every program connected to Cuebot's built-in WebSocket address (the one other apps use to talk to Cuebot).

fields.message: The text to send. If it is written as JSON it is sent as data, otherwise as plain text.

variables.sentCount: How many programs got the message

core.httpRequest.description: Visits a web address and saves the answer. Use it to call other websites or tools, like fetching a joke or poking a smart device.

fields.method: GET asks for information. POST sends information. PUT, PATCH and DELETE change or remove things on the other side. HEAD asks only for the headline details.
fields.url: The full web address, starting with http:// or https://, like "https://example.com/api".
fields.headers: Extra details sent along, one per line as "Name: value". Most people can leave this empty.
fields.body: The data to send with a POST, PUT or PATCH. Leave empty if you send nothing.
fields.contentType: What kind of data the body is. application/json is right for JSON. Only used when there is a body.
fields.timeout: How many seconds to wait for an answer before giving up. The most is 30.
fields.variable: The name of the variable that will hold the answer. Use it later as %httpResponse% (or the name you type).
fields.parseJson: Tick if the answer is JSON data. Each value in it also gets its own variable, like %httpResponse.name%.

variables.httpResponse: The answer text (or the name you chose in the box above)
variables.httpStatusCode: The result number: 200 means it worked, 404 means not found
variables.httpHeaders: The extra details that came back
variables.httpError: What went wrong, if the request failed or timed out

core.udpBroadcast.description: Sends a short text message to other devices on your network, or to this computer, with no reply expected. Handy for small gadgets or other apps that listen.

fields.port: The door number the other app listens on, from 1 to 65535. Check that app's settings.
fields.host: Who to send it to. 255.255.255.255 shouts to every device on your home network. 127.0.0.1 means this computer. You can also type one device's address.
